title: Daniyal Mansur, Founder and CEO of 22 Signals
description: Daniyal Mansur is the founder and CEO of 22 Signals, a global business solutions company based in London, working across AI, technology and growth.
intro: Daniyal Mansur is the founder and CEO of 22 Signals, a global business solutions company based in London. He sets the company's direction, works directly with clients on what to build first, and still builds some of 22 Signals' AI tools himself.

list: Distinction|MSc Business Analytics, Queen Mary University of London

p: Daniyal leads 22 Signals from London. He spends most of his time with clients, working out which problem is worth solving first and what it will take, then hands the work to the specialist teams with one accountable lead and dates in writing.
He still builds some of the company's AI tools himself. It keeps him close to what the team actually delivers, and it means the advice clients get on AI comes from someone who has shipped it.

He launched Salt Esports in 2019, at 17, and grew it to a million followers, with brand partnerships with brands such as Red Bull, Unilever and Daraz. In 2022 Salt became the first team from Pakistan at the Commonwealth Esports Championships.
Building a brand and an audience from nothing taught him the marketing side of a business: what makes people pay attention, and what makes them stay.
He went on to help run large live events for brands including Tencent and Garena, among them Galaxy Racer 2024, which drew more than 20,000 attendees.
Live events have one rule: the start time never moves. That habit carried straight into 22 Signals, where every date agreed with a client goes in writing.

Daniyal holds an MSc in Business Analytics with Distinction from Queen Mary University of London, and a BBA from the Lahore School of Economics. On the MSc he led a process-mining project on how orders turn into cash.
It shaped how 22 Signals works: look at how a business actually runs, with real data, before deciding what to build.
